original_clauses.source_paraphrase: The sheriff’s office said its review found that several credentialed employees searched plate-location records for personal or other non-law-enforcement purposes, including a coworker lookup. The reported matters span different employees and dates; the record does not establish that they acted together.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Search access granted for law-enforcement work must remain limited to queries supported by that purpose; authenticated access does not authorize a personal search or repurpose collected location data.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The reported users had technical access but allegedly searched for purposes outside their delegated query authority.
Data collected for law enforcement was allegedly reused for materially different personal purposes without an independent basis.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: The agency’s internal review and continuing audits surfaced separate employee cases, leading to employment and criminal-process actions; the reviewed record does not disclose the full query logs or final legal outcomes.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: An oversight process should be able to identify anomalous access and preserve a traceable basis for later review; detection does not by itself establish every disputed search or guilt.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: After the fourth case, the sheriff’s office reported revising policy to include at least twice-yearly audits, access limits, user certification and training; effectiveness of these changes has not been reported.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Remedial safeguards need to constrain future searches in operation; announcing policy changes does not establish that they have been implemented or effective.
